review.tagline: Context database that stores agent memory, resources and skills as a virtual filesystem
review.summary: OpenViking organizes what an agent knows under a viking:// virtual filesystem, with documents, memories and skills browsable through ls, tree, read, write and grep. Directories carry generated L0 abstracts and L1 overviews so agents read summaries before full content, and committed sessions become editable Markdown memories. It ships a server, an ov CLI, Python, Go and TypeScript SDKs, an HTTP API, and a memory plugin installer for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others.
review.audience: Developers giving coding agents persistent, inspectable memory and context
strengths: Memory is stored as inspectable, editable files under viking:// URIs rather than opaque embeddings
Search can be scoped to a directory subtree; L0/L1 summaries cut full reads
Plugin installer covers Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, TRAE, OpenCode, with OpenClaw and Hermes integrations
Python, Go and TypeScript SDKs, HTTP API, CLI, plus accounts, user isolation and opt-in ACLs
weaknesses: AGPL-3.0 license may constrain embedding in proprietary or networked products
Needs a model provider with both an embedding model and a VLM
Memory extraction runs in the background, so new memories are not immediately retrievable
Published benchmarks use Volcengine Doubao models; results with other providers are not shown
needs: Needs uv, Python 3.10+, Embedding model provider, VLM provider, Node.js 18+ (plugin installer)
Models: Volcengine, OpenAI, Codex OAuth, Kimi, GLM
